messages.content: Write a polished short scene in modern American English that is mostly dialogue between two adult friends making plans for the weekend. Let them occasionally talk past each other, correct each other, and misunderstand small things. Keep the conversation coherent without making every line perfectly efficient. Use only enough action to ground the exchange.

“Saturday?”

“Maybe.”

“You said Sunday.”

“I said Saturday might work.”

“You said Sunday first.”

“Because you asked about Sunday.”

“I asked about the weekend.”

“Which includes Sunday.”

“It also includes Saturday.”

“I know how weekends work.”

“Just checking.”

Casey folded the receipt on the counter into a smaller square.

“So what are you actually asking?”

“Do you want to go?”

“Where?”

Morgan stared at her.

“You know.”

“No. I genuinely don't.”

“The market.”

“What market?”

“The one we've been talking about all week.”

“We've been talking about three markets.”

Morgan stopped.

“There are three?”

“Yes.”

Casey pulled out her phone.

“The farmer's market, the antique market, and that weird one with all the handmade furniture.”

“The weird one is the one I meant.”

“I don't think you ever said that.”

“I thought I did.”

“You didn't.”

Morgan leaned against the counter.

“Fine. The weird furniture market.”

“What time?”

“I don't know.”

“Where is it?”

“I don't know.”

Casey looked up.

“Then you have done almost no planning.”

“I had a concept.”

“A concept.”

“Yes.”

“That isn't a plan.”

“I know.”

Casey smiled.

“Saturday.”

Morgan nodded. “Saturday.”

“And we'll figure out the rest.”

“That's basically how I planned it.”

“Sure.”
